predicates: The invented primary script is well formed. Given any of its full typed valuations, the prefix lookup/call of relay returns the selected Boolean. The unused-constant lookup returns the supplied integer. Correct behavior is required through the original names, function environments and interpreter, without replacing source calls by a supplied truth table.

The actual full evaluator returns some [b,!b] on every valuation, including all integers. Its output is invariant when only the omitted integer changes. Both Boolean leaves feed an independently typed finite aggregate which proves that at least one ordered result is false.

A constructive pair with retained bit true and omitted integers 0 and 1 has equal projections, different complete prefix environments and equal successful full outputs. The changed-assertion program reads the integer, giving [true,false] and [false,true] respectively. The malformed program gives none.
